snippet.textDisplay: My mom had dementia and we had her do important things. I did make the mistake of giving her a pull-up to put on herself, I was busy. When she came out of the bathroom, she was wearing it as a hat. I gave her junk mail to open, had her sort buttons, or colored cotton balls. The buttons and cotton balls were smooth and soft. The sensation seemed to soothe her. You have to laugh or cry at some of the things that happen. We chose to laugh, and it also helped her to smile.

snippet.textDisplay: My dad has covered up my mom's dementia, he is 93 and she'll be 90 in a month. It is very, very bad. I'm living with them now and she can't get past about a minute without asking the same question which is usually where she is. A half hour ago she asked where her husband was to my dad whom she just celebrated 69 years married a few days ago. I find that giving her jewelry which is something she made many years of her life, plays with now and😢 redirects her. It keeps her focused. I also noticed when a traumatic event happens like when my dad falls, she does know where she is.

snippet.textDisplay: My Mom kept packing to go home and would go stand at her current home's carport door, with her suitcase, Sunday coat, hat, purse and matching shoes.   Everyone argued with her and  laughed.  One day I asked her, "Mom, if you want to go home, where do you live?  She gave me her address where she lived as a young girl.  She said Momma will be worried about me and I must get home.  I do not remember her asking again.    We never found all her bathcloths.  Maybe they were in the suitcase?  I miss her soo much ❤ and can hardly wait to see her again in Heaven ❤  She has dementia from falling, picking flowers.  Before her jarred  brain healed, she fell again.  She did go to rehab for 3 weeks, started back walking and doing things around the house, BUT never completely recovered.  Dr. Said when she fell, it was like a football play hit and before her brain healed and recovered, she fell again.  There are alot of football players who develop memory and learning difficulties because they do not WAIT to heal before playing sports again.  We must use our common sense GOD YAHWEH has given us. 😊❤

snippet.textDisplay:
It’s not your imagination. You ARE breaking. Before you snap, consider this: You must stay healthy and strong. Keep some time for yourself alone, seek help and comfort from other life helpers, have an outlet or hobby that provides a creative expression, even if that’s adult coloring books.

Your mind can either be your best friend or your worst enemy. Fill it with ideas and gentle thoughts. Be as good to yourself as you are to your charge.

snippet.textDisplay:
My mother’s husband hated all of her repetitive behaviours and was always saying “no” and correcting her. You could tell she hated it.
When I was with her we just did what she wanted over and over again like it was the first time. It was about her and her journey and no matter how far along they are “no” and “stop that” is upsetting, just like it is for the rest of us 🤷🏼‍♂️
Only time we had to redirect was if she was doing something that wasn’t going to end well, but most of the time it was harmless stuff. Be present for that person and give them what they need.

Yeah, that worked for a little while. Now she doubles down on insisting she can and has done whatever it is we're trying to stop her from doing for 60 some years! Listing every damn thing she did for her family, correctly and accurately. She knows when we are trying to redirect most of the time now, then proceeds to be in a negative mood for days or weeks. It's exhausting.
The problem seems to be that she is aware most of the time of what's happening, but of course, her short-term memory is not good, which makes her angry. She will not admit she has a problem and feels we are all trying to take over her home, which, of course, makes her angry and suspicious of everyone!

snippet.textDisplay:
​@marypoppins2023Thank you. Mom has since passed away and I am grateful for the years I was able to assist in her caregiving. As hard as it was to watch this woman who was the North Star to me suffer the indignity of dementia, I will always be grateful for the time I shared with her. The good and the bad.
I hope you grant yourself grace through this difficult time. One of the most important things I learned from this channel was to always try and leave your family member with a smile whenever possible!!! They will associate being happy with you. It helped me so much as we neared her end.
I never told anyone, but just days before she passed, she hugged me and told me I was home to her. In my world, she was home to all of us, so that made me feel like I had given her the love and support she needed. I will carry that with me through the rest of my own life. 🙏

My 85 yo mom fell many times and has fractures that just couldn’t healed due to constantly bedridden due to falls, in and out of hospitals. So right now she is unable to walk. Even with a walker, it is a struggle. She hasn’t fall in 2 months and legs are getting a bit stronger. So she yelled and screamed at the helper when helper asked her to use the walker. So the helper had to walk behind her to catch her should she falls. She literally pushed the helper away when asked. It is a huge issue since she will fall again if her legs gave out. She is unable to take more than 5 steps on her own and she needed to hang on to door, chair or sofa to accomplishes that 5 steps. We are dealing with a very difficult old lady. She is very spoiled, controlling and extremely difficult all her life and now it is just getting worse by the day. Previous helper already quit and so we now have another helper who is just 3 weeks into the job. I expected her to quit shortly due to the daily verbal abuse from my mom. What can I do to encourage her to use the walker? We tried explaining to her and she threw a hissy fit telling us that her condition isn’t as serious as what everybody is saying. I don’t want to send her to a nursing home but we can’t keep changing helpers. So much money and time involved. I hope that she can live out the rest of her life at home but it really doesn’t look like it can happen with her being disobedient and defiant in everything especially when it is safety. I don’t live in the same country as her but with technology and many CCTVs around the house, I am very involved in her day to day care and her doctor’s visits. I am currently training the new helper as well. I can only visit her for 2-3 months per visit and so she isn’t keen in listening to what I have to say.
Any tips anyone? Thank you!

snippet.textDisplay: As a caregiver, what would be most helpful for me is having someone show me how to dress my husband.  It's becoming so frustrating for me.  He no longer understands words like "lift your leg" or "pull up".  I have had to go with shirts that are button up instead of pull over the head.  I had to do away with belts and jeans a year ago and go with elastic waist band sweats pants in winter and thin pajama pants in summer, and short socks instead of the tube socks he used to wear.  But just getting all his clothes on him is challenging. I am a foot shorter than he.

snippet.textDisplay: @savinggrace-s2b for pants/shorts, I have him sit down and pat/tap on his leg....same.for socks. For shirts, I hold open the bottom of the shirt and he puts his arms in, then I slip the neck/collar over his head. For belts, he stands still & allows me to put the belt thru the loops, if not & too confused, I put the belt thru the loops prior to putting on his pants. Hope this helps you... 🙏 ❤️. Always say , good job & thank  you to him.

snippet.textDisplay:
Another good tip is when they asked about a dead relative.
And you know to tell them the truth would upset them.
Always say, "You are not well, you have forgotten but when your memory comes back again you will remember."
Never say they ard still around because if you do they will get more muddled and just keep on asking.
We found this worked a treat and my friend wouldn't ask anymore but actually remembered they had passed away amd didn't ask again.
I think living in the moment is very important for dementia patients.
Sending love and hugs to uour channel, love your tips too.
❤

snippet.textDisplay:
You could say the same thing about children doing something you don't want them to. Like watching a TV show you think is inappropriate... have something ready to entice them with in case of situations like that. While they're busy with the distraction, have someone change the channel. While any disapproved show is on the air, engage the child in some fun time. Telling the child you don't want them to watch a certain show will make them resent you.

Basically, treat children like dementia patients.
